title: Cheat Sheet

lessons.title: Course Material: Cheat-Sheet.pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Keep Your Customers for Life – Cheat Sheet  Introduction  ü The most successful business use marketing strategies that keep customers around for life  ü They focus on building long-term relationships and loyalty ü Nurture your existing customers to increase their lifetime value and ensure healthy business growth ü Customer retention is more cost effective than customer acquisition ü Reengage with lost customers and be open to their feedback ü Reconnect with them and remind them of your offers – you’ll be surprised by the results ü Enhance your retention and reengagement strategies with Customer Lifecycle Marketing ü Establish a successful Customers for Life strategy   Learning Objectives:  ü Identify the phases of the Customer Lifecycle Marketing Model and how it enables you to keep customers for life  ü Collect data that shows your customers’ buying behaviors over time, so that you have objective information to inform your marketing decisions ü Gather feedback from customers about why they stay and why they leave, so you can plan effective strategies for retention and reengagement

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  ü Gain a deeper understanding of what’s important to your customers, so that you continue to provide appropriate solutions to their problems  ü Choose practical tactics to keep your ideal customers happy, so that they will want to stay with you and refer you to others ü Gain a deeper understanding of why some customers leave, so you can identify what will reignite their interest and bring them back  ü Decide which practical tactics you will use to successfully bring former customers back into your business orbit, so you can target future opportunities to them   ü Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps     Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Module 1 – How Customer Lifecycle Marketing Gives You Customers for Life  Key Takeaways: Ø Customer Lifecycle Marketing improves your return on investment by increasing the lifetime value of a customer.  Ø It’s more cost-effective to market to existing and former customers than to find new ones, so focus your energy on keeping your customers for life.  Learning Objective: ü Identify the phases of the Customer Lifecycle Marketing Model and how it enables you to keep customers for life   Keep Customers at Every Stage ü If you use sales funnels, your focus isn’t on retaining customers ü Once the sale is made, there’s no provision for follow-up ü You may have let repeat customers slip through the net ü Keeping existing customers is more cost-effective than attracting new ones ü Adopt the 3-phase Customer Lifecycle Marketing Model ü It integrates your marketing tactics and helps you keep customers engaged with you over time ü Each phase has two marketing objectives ü Engagement forms the center or ‘hub’ that keeps the cycle moving, making it dynamic

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  
              Phase 1 Attract- make consumers aware of your brand and your offers and help them identify their needs ü Develop awareness - This is your chance to inform people about your business and educate them on your topic of expertise.  ü Explore needs- help customers identify what their needs really are.   Phase 2 Motivate – educate and help customers evaluate your offers, take action to purchase and stay in touch. ü Offer solutions - Provide information about your offers and reinforce how your solution meets your customers’ needs  ü Encourage action - Customers are now ready to take action, and they need you to tell them what to do. If they aren’t ready just now, keep them in the cycle until they are ready

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  Phase 3 Delight – deliver exceptional customer support for those who bought, and provide experiences that turn happy customers into loyal brand advocates.  ü Support customers - First-class customer support helps you retain your customers, gets you repeat business, and sets you apart from the competition. ü Build loyalty -Maximize customer satisfaction and engage those happy customers so that they generate more business for you.   ü With Customer Lifecycle Marketing, your customers are engaged throughout the cycle, no matter whether they buy this time or not  Where Does Customer Retention and Reengagement Fit In? ü If you use Customer Lifecycle Marketing, your focus shifts from the one-off sale to the long-term relationship  ü It encourages your customers to continue buying products and services from your business ü Your aim is to build your customer base for life ü Retaining the customers you already have gives a better return on your marketing investment ü Bringing back former customers also makes business sense  ü This course focuses more on the Delight phase than the other two phases in the model - i.e. the post-purchase phase ü Businesses fail to delight and lose customers for different reasons: o Quality of product o Communication o Slow response to questions

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  o Lack of information o Technical issues o Lack of support o Over promotion ü In Delight phase, you can provide the vital elements that keep customers for life: o Exceptional customer service o Customer-exclusive rewards o VIP treatment ü You can entice customers back into the fold, from the beginning of the cycle through to the end: o Match your solutions to customer needs which might have changed since they bought from you last o Anticipate the customer’s objections o Encourage customers to take action. ü Adopting the Customer Lifecycle Marketing Model gives you a comprehensive way to retain and reengage customers ü Complete the Customers for Life Checklist to identify gaps in your marketing provision ü It’s a snapshot of today’s situation and a starting point for your customer retention and reengagement strategies   Action Steps: 1. Complete the separate Customers for Life Checklist to identify your starting point with customer retention and reengagement. 2. Note down where you have found gaps in your provision from the Checklist.

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  Module 2 – Your Current Situation Lesson 1: Know Your Customer Stats  Key Takeaways: Ø There are some basic customer stats you need to know as a business owner. Don’t shy away from them. Ø They help you understand your business and plan for future growth.  Learning Objective: ü Collect data that shows your customers’ buying behaviors over time, so that you have objective information to inform your marketing decisions Know your numbers ü Before you can plan any changes, you need to know the details of your current situation  ü You need to know some basic numbers about your business ü Successful entrepreneurs have these figures readily available  1. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) ü Customer acquisition cost (CAC) will show you how much it costs you to attract each new customer 2. Lifetime Value (LTV) ü Lifetime value (LTV) will reveal how much a customer is worth to you throughout their time with you

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  3. LTV:CAC Ratio ü Work out your LTV:CAC ratio to give you an idea if your return is healthy or not 4. Customer Return Rate ü Customer return rate will show how many customers you’ve retained over a period of time, e.g. a year, 6 months, etc. 5. Percentage of Lost & Retained Customers ü You need to know the percentage of lost customers so you can monitor your figures  ü There will always be some movement in customer numbers ü Once you’ve done this math, use it to draw conclusions about the goals you should set    Action Steps: 1. Calculate your numbers using the formulae given in the lesson: a. Customer acquisition cost b. Lifetime value c. Lifetime value to customer acquisition cost ratio d. Customer return rate or % of customers who bought more than once e. % of lost customers & % of retained customers 2. What conclusions can you draw from these statistics?

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  Lesson 2: Know Your Customer’s “Why?”   Key Takeaways: Ø Gather data to gain important insight into why some customers stay with you and why others leave. Ø If you use customer satisfaction surveys, make sure you set specific goals for what you want to do with the information you receive.   Learning Objective: ü Gather your customer data, so that you can identify why customers stay and why they leave and plan strategies accordingly  Collect Qualitative Data ü Find out what makes some customers happy and continue buying from you, and why others choose to leave  ü You may already have this data from: o Testimonials o Comments on social media o Customer reviews o Personal emails, messages, and letters o Past surveys o Analytics ü Arrange to call some of your customers, both satisfied and dissatisfied ü Unhappy customers will help you pinpoint weak areas in your business and places for improvement

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  Use Customer Satisfaction Surveys ü Many businesses use customer satisfaction surveys to keep customers happy and improve their services  What is Customer Satisfaction? ü The customer’s perception of whether they were satisfied that they got what they paid for ü Define the term for yourself so you know what you want to measure with your survey ü When you’ve chosen what you’re measuring, you then need to decide: o What type of survey will give you that data? o When is the best time to send it? o To whom do you send it? ü Make the survey fun, inviting, and quick to fill in ü Two popular survey types: o Questionnaire type – mix of closed and open questions o Ratings type – customer responds with a numerical rating (e.g. 1-10) ü Ask questions while it still matters and w
